title: Motion and states
instruction: Keep motion under the reader’s control, and give every state visible text.
intro: Motion here means a mark that moves on screen to show a change, such as a bill reaching its next step or a link forming between a cause and its effect. A state is how a control or a region looks while something about it holds, from a focus ring to an error. This chapter sets how a motion runs and how each state looks, and chapter 18 says where each component uses them.

A reader starts every motion, and a reader whose device asks for less motion sees the last frame at once. Every state shows words or a shape as well as a color, on Newsprint and on Charcoal, so it reads in gray print, in a dark theme and to a reader who sees no color.

groups.title: Motion under the reader’s control
groups.line: A motion explains a change, keeps to nine timing tokens and starts only when a reader asks.

groups.title: Three behaviors, and the identity’s own
groups.line: Slide, draw and land build every motion, and the hinge and the lever keep motions of their own.

groups.title: States
groups.line: Each state shows words or a shape as well as a color, on Newsprint and on Charcoal.

rules.title: Move something only to explain a state or a mechanism.
rule: Motion has two jobs. It shows a state changing, as when a bill finishes one step and moves to the next, and it shows a mechanism at work, as when a link draws from a cause to its effect. A mark that would move for any other reason, to decorate a page or to catch the eye, stays still.
A reader’s own actions, such as a hover, a toggle or a change of theme, answer at once or within the fast duration, 120 ms. The focus ring shows at once, with no motion at all.

text: A moving mark draws the eye before the words around it, so a motion with no change behind it takes a reader away from the sentence they came to read. For some readers motion costs more than attention. The W3C’s Media Queries Level 5 says the motion a reduced motion setting removes can “trigger discomfort for those with vestibular motion sensitivity, or distraction for those with attention deficits.” The vestibular sense is the inner ear’s sense of balance and motion.
why.basis: Design judgment, with the W3C’s Media Queries Level 5

correct.caption: Live. Press Play and bill S.99002 moves from step 3, Committee vote, to step 4, First chamber. Step 3 lands as done, then the ring that marks where the bill is now slides to step 4 and draws the line behind it. Every part of the motion shows something that changed.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 17.1. A count rises from 0 to 1,284 as the page opens. Nothing changed for the reader: the number was known before the page drew, and the motion makes them wait for it.

specs.label: A state changes
specs.value: A step finishes; a bill moves on; a mark arrives at its new state

specs.label: A mechanism works
specs.value: A link draws from cause to effect; the current step of a loop moves on

specs.label: A reader’s own action
specs.value: Hover and toggles at once or in 120 ms; the focus ring at once

specs.label: Leave out
specs.value: Autoplaying video, looping animation, parallax, motion tied to scrolling, bounce or elastic easing, animated gradients, confetti, counters that tick up and hover that moves layout

builders: Before you add a motion, write the sentence it shows, such as “Step 3 is done and the bill is now at step 4.” If no change gives you that sentence, leave the mark still.
Keep native scrolling. Tie no motion to the scroll position, and take nothing over from the wheel or the keys that scroll the page.

rules.title: Time every motion with the nine motion tokens.
rule: Every duration and easing in a motion comes from a token: three durations for most moves, a 40 ms stagger between marks that move one after another, two durations kept for the hinge and the lever, and three easings. A motion reads them from tokens.css by name, so a reduced motion setting reaches it (Rule 17.4).

Hover and toggles take the fast duration, 120 ms. Reveals, panels, a mark that lands and a line that draws on its own take the standard 200 ms, and a move across a page or a component takes the slow 320 ms. The easing follows where a mark goes: the enter easing for a mark that arrives, the exit easing at the fast duration for one that leaves, and the standard easing for one that moves from place to place.

text: These are our fifth edition’s values, kept as they were. Nothing in the set runs longer than 680 ms, so a motion is over before a reader’s eye moves on. The three easings slow down into place, or speed away from it, and none passes its place and comes back, so a mark rests exactly where the still view draws it.
why.basis: Design judgment, kept from our fifth edition

correct.caption: The nine tokens. The six durations share one scale, with the hinge’s 680 ms across its full width, and each easing is drawn as its curve.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 17.2. A transition written with its own numbers. A reduced motion setting never reaches 250 ms, and the curve goes 10 percent past its place before it comes back.

specs.label: Fast
specs.value: 120 ms; hover and toggles

specs.label: Standard
specs.value: 200 ms; reveals, panels, a land, a draw on its own

specs.label: Slow
specs.value: 320 ms; a move across a page or a component

specs.label: Stagger
specs.value: 40 ms between marks that move one after another

specs.label: Hinge
specs.value: 680 ms, on request only (Rule 17.6)

specs.label: Lever
specs.value: 560 ms, on request only (Rule 17.6)

specs.label: Standard easing
specs.value: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1); a move from place to place

specs.label: Enter easing
specs.value: cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1); a mark that arrives

specs.label: Exit easing
specs.value: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1); a mark that leaves, at the fast duration

builders: Write transition: transform var(--oa-motion-duration-standard) var(--oa-motion-easing-enter), never the number. A script reads the same names with getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue('--oa-motion-duration-slow'), which gives 320ms, or 0ms under reduced motion.

rules.title: Play a motion only when a reader asks.
rule: Every player has Play, Pause, Reset and a still view, and a motion starts only when a reader presses Play, never as the page opens, as it scrolls into view or on a timer. It runs once and stops on its last frame. One button carries Play and Pause and changes its icon and its word together, then reads Play again at the end.

A player of a state or a mechanism rests on its first frame, where the change starts. For the wordmark or the lockmark, the player rests on the master itself, so a reader who never presses Play still sees the whole mark; Play then steps to the first frame and runs to the master. Reset, named for what it resets, such as “Reset the bill” (Rule 11.14), takes either kind back to where it rests, and at rest it is unavailable and says why.

Beside every player sits its still view: the first and last frames at true size, each with its time and the words for what it shows, then each step of the motion in order. A status line says the same words when the frame changes, so every fact the motion shows reaches a reader who prints the page or listens with a screen reader, and one who never presses Play.

text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide asks for a way to pause anything that starts on its own and moves for more than five seconds. Our motions last under a second and never start on their own, so none needs it. Every player has the controls all the same, and a reader decides when each mark moves. Slow motion stretches a motion to a few seconds, which gives Pause time to work and lets a reader see the easing.

correct.caption: The parts of a player, numbered from top to bottom, drawn from the live player in Rule 17.4. It shows a mechanism, so it rests on its first frame. Each part has its words, and the controls stand 44 px tall.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 17.3. The bill moves as the page opens and again every three seconds, so it seems to go back and forth between two steps. Its one button has an icon and no word, and there is no Pause, Reset or still view.

specs.label: Play and Pause
specs.value: One button; its icon and word change together: Play, Pause, Play again

specs.label: At rest
specs.value: A state or a mechanism: its first frame. The wordmark or the lockmark: its master

specs.label: Reset
specs.value: Named for what it resets, such as “Reset the bill”; takes the player back to where it rests; unavailable at rest, with its reason

specs.label: Slow motion
specs.value: A check box that plays at one tenth speed; unavailable under reduced motion, with its reason

specs.label: Still view
specs.value: First and last frames at true size, each with its time and words, then the steps in order

specs.label: Status line
specs.value: Polite, so a screen reader waits until it finishes speaking; it says Playing, Paused and the words of the frame the motion stops on

specs.label: Controls
specs.value: 44 px tall, with 24 px icons beside their words

specs.label: Runs
specs.value: Once for each press; never on load, on scroll or on a timer; never loops

builders: Mark the player’s root data-oa-motion, its one Play and Pause button data-oa-play data-oa-pause and Reset data-oa-reset; the guide’s own check looks for them. A player that rests on its master also takes data-oa-rest="master" and loads with data-frame="end". Start a motion from a click handler and nowhere else.
Leave the last frame on screen when the motion ends. On load, draw a state or mechanism player at its first frame, and a player of the wordmark or the lockmark at its master.

rules.title: Under reduced motion, show the last frame at once.
rule: When a reader’s device asks for reduced motion, every motion duration token resolves to 0 ms, and pressing Play draws the last frame at once. The player keeps its buttons and its words, so the reader still chooses when the change shows and reads in the status line what changed.

tokens.css does this itself, with the media query prefers-reduced-motion, which every current browser supports. A motion that reads its timing from the tokens follows the setting with no code of its own.

text: The W3C’s Media Queries Level 5 says the reduce value “Indicates that user has notified the system that they prefer an interface that removes or replaces the types of motion-based animation that either trigger discomfort for those with vestibular motion sensitivity, or distraction for those with attention deficits.” Drawing the last frame keeps every fact the motion shows and removes the movement alone.
why.basis: Media Queries Level 5, W3C Working Draft, February 19, 2026

correct.caption: Live. The first link of Loop R1 from our systems atlas draws from concentration of household wealth to money spent to influence politics, and the arrowhead and the second node land. Turn on Preview reduced motion, or set your device to reduce motion, and Play draws the last frame at once. The line under the check boxes says what your device asks for now.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 17.4. A script times its own 400 ms. The setting reaches tokens.css, which the script never reads, so a reader who asked for reduced motion still watches the link draw.

specs.label: Durations
specs.value: All six resolve to 0 ms: fast, standard, slow, stagger, hinge and lever

specs.label: Easings
specs.value: Unchanged; at 0 ms they have no effect

specs.label: Media query
specs.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), already in tokens.css

specs.label: Controls
specs.value: Kept: Play draws the last frame and Reset the first; Slow motion is unavailable, with its reason

specs.label: Browsers
specs.value: First full support: Chrome 74, Edge 79, Firefox 63, Safari 10.1, Safari on iOS 10.3, by MDN’s compatibility data, checked November 10, 2026

builders: In a script, read the duration at the moment of the press: parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue('--oa-motion-duration-slow')) gives 320, or 0 under reduced motion. When every duration is 0, set the last frame and start no animation.
To check a page, turn on reduced motion in your device settings, or in Chrome’s developer tools under Rendering, “Emulate CSS media feature prefers-reduced-motion”, and press every Play.

rules.title: Build every motion from three behaviors: slide, draw and land.
rule: A slide moves a mark from one place to another along a straight line, over the slow duration with the standard easing. A draw extends a line along its own path from its start, over the standard duration with the enter easing, and a line drawn behind a sliding mark takes the slide’s duration and easing so the two keep pace. A land brings a mark to rest: it appears at 112 percent of its size and settles to its true size over the standard duration with the enter easing.

A motion may join two or three of them in order, one stagger apart, as a bill does when its step lands and its ring slides on (Rule 17.1). Nothing in a behavior fades, since no state uses opacity, and nothing passes its place and comes back.

text: Our fifth edition named these three behaviors and timed them, and this edition keeps both. It sets the size a land starts from at 112 percent, the step our fifth edition’s lever took when it landed at 1.4 times a node and settled at 1.25, so every land in our products keeps that one proportion. A reader who has seen a ring slide to a bill’s next step reads the same slide in a loop on the atlas.
why.basis: Design judgment, kept and refined from our fifth edition

correct.caption: Live. Each behavior on its own: a ring slides from one place to the next, a line draws from its first node to its second, and a disc lands on its node. Slow motion plays each at one tenth speed.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 17.5. A disc lands with a bounce. It shrinks, swells past its node and shrinks again, so it sits at four sizes before it rests, and the extra movement says nothing about the state.

specs.label: Slide
specs.value: 320 ms, standard easing; a straight line between two places

specs.label: Draw
specs.value: 200 ms, enter easing; behind a slide, the slide’s duration and easing

specs.label: Land
specs.value: 200 ms, enter easing; from 112 percent to true size

specs.label: Together
specs.value: In order, 40 ms apart

specs.label: Leaving
specs.value: A mark that leaves: the exit easing at 120 ms

specs.label: What moves
specs.value: A mark’s place, the length of a drawn line and a mark’s size; never opacity, never layout

builders: Animate transform and stroke-dashoffset only, so the text around a mark never moves. Give a drawn line pathLength="1" and stroke-dasharray="1 1", then move stroke-dashoffset from 1 to 0 to draw it whole at any length.

rules.title: Move the hinge and the lever only as their own motions.
rule: The hinge and the lever are the two motions that belong to the identity, and each one plays only on request (Rule 17.3) and ends exactly on its master. The hinge plays over 680 ms: OATH and ACTION settle into place, then the ampersand lands between them. The lever plays over 560 ms in the lockmark: its links draw, its nodes land together and the lever lands last, at bottom right.

Each player rests on the master itself (Rule 17.3). Play steps to the first frame and runs to the master, and Reset returns to the master; at rest Reset is unavailable, with the line “The mark is at rest on its master. Reset works once you press Play.”

Each is built from slide, draw and land (Rule 17.5), and each ends on a last frame that matches the approved master for its size, pixel for pixel. The ampersand and the lever keep signature red in every frame, and signature red never counts as a view’s working red (Rule 05.3).

text: The hinge and the lever carry our name and our idea of a place where one change moves the rest, so a reader who sees them move should see them arrive as the same drawings they meet everywhere else. A last frame a pixel off its master would show a second version of the mark.

correct.caption: Live, at rest on the wordmark’s master. Press Play, and OATH and ACTION start apart, settle into place over 320 ms, then the ampersand lands between them and comes to rest at 680 ms, on the master again. The master stands at 24 px and, on a wide screen, at 64 px.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 17.6. Last frames that come to rest half a pixel low, because the player centers each mark with a transform in a box one pixel taller than the mark. On a 1x screen the lockmark’s links turn into gray bands and the wordmark goes soft, so each last frame is a second version of its mark.

specs.label: Hinge
specs.value: 680 ms in all, on request: OATH and ACTION slide toward each other over the slow 320 ms, and the ampersand lands from 480 ms and comes to rest at 680 ms

specs.label: Lever
specs.value: 560 ms in all, on request: the links draw over 200 ms, the nodes land together from 240 ms, and the lever lands from 360 ms and comes to rest at 560 ms

specs.label: Built from
specs.value: Slide, draw and land, with the enter easing for each arrival

specs.label: At rest
specs.value: The master; Reset unavailable, with “The mark is at rest on its master. Reset works once you press Play.”

specs.label: Last frame
specs.value: The approved master for the size shown, pixel for pixel

specs.label: Reduced motion
specs.value: The master at once (Rule 17.4)

builders: Animate the master itself, never a redrawn copy, and compare the last frame with the master at its size before it ships.

When the motion ends, show the master file itself, placed as Rules 03.1 and 08.1 place it, so the last frame is the master. Check the last frame on a 1x screen, since a 2x screen hides a mark that rests half a pixel off the grid.

rules.title: Show loading with words and a still drawing, never a pulse.
rule: While a region waits for its data, it shows words that name what is loading, such as “Loading the tracker for S.99002.” Illustrative, and a still drawing of the lines the data will sit on, with no marks on them yet. The words sit in a status line, so a screen reader hears them once. Nothing moves while the region waits.
The data replaces the drawing and the words together. When the data fails to arrive, the region shows the error state with what failed and the fix (Rule 11.15).

text: A pulse repeats for as long as the wait lasts, which puts it under WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide once the wait passes five seconds. Our fifth edition’s pulsing lever also fell to 1.27 to 1 against Newsprint at its faintest, under the 3 to 1 that success criterion 1.4.11 asks of a graphic a reader needs. Words say what is happening, and a screen reader can say them too. The drawing leaves out marks, because a step or a node on it would read as a state the data has not reached.

correct.caption: A tracker that is loading, on Newsprint and on Charcoal. The line where the six steps will sit measures 4.29 to 1 on Newsprint and 7.26 on Charcoal, and the words name the bill.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 17.7. Our fifth edition’s loading pulse, in still frames. It fades between 20 and 50 percent strength for as long as the wait lasts, and nothing says what is loading.

specs.label: Words
specs.value: What is loading, by name, in a status line

specs.label: Drawing
specs.value: The lines the data will sit on, with no marks; 4.29 to 1 on Newsprint

specs.label: On Charcoal
specs.value: Dim Newsprint words and drawing, 7.26 to 1

specs.label: Motion
specs.value: None, with or without reduced motion

specs.label: When it fails
specs.value: The error state, with what failed and the fix (Rule 11.15)

builders: Put an empty element with role="status" on the page before the data is asked for, then write the words into it, so a screen reader hears them.

rules.title: Give all ten states words or a shape as well as a color.
rule: Ten states cover every control and region, on Newsprint and on Charcoal: muted, disabled, hover, focus, loading, selected, warning, error, empty and success. Each changes its words or its shape along with its color, so a reader who sees no color, prints in gray or reads in a dark theme gets the same state. This plate is the reference for all ten.

On Charcoal an error takes no band: the 4 px Pillar Red bar measures 4.49 to 1 there, and the mark and the word “Error:” in Newsprint carry it. Every other state keeps the same shapes and words on both surfaces.

text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 1.4.1 Use of Color asks that color never be the only way a state shows, and 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast asks 3 to 1 for the edges, marks and rings that show one. Each sample here reads only the short names, which a theme points at Newsprint’s values or Charcoal’s, so one set of code draws both columns, and a product that follows a reader’s theme changes its colors and keeps its words and shapes.

correct.caption: The ten states, each on Newsprint and on Charcoal, with its cue in words. Each cell sets its own theme, and every color in it comes from a short name that follows the theme.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 17.8. Four states by color alone. The red words measure 2.96 to 1 and the Verdigris words 3.37, and a reader who sees neither color gets no state at all; the faded button falls to 2.48 and gives no reason.

specs.label: Muted
specs.value: Secondary words in regular weight; outline marks, 4.29 to 1 on Newsprint

specs.label: Disabled
specs.value: Dashed edge, words at 5.49 to 1 on Newsprint and 7.26 on Charcoal, a reason line (Rule 17.11)

specs.label: Hover
specs.value: Underline or a 2 px edge; a filled button steps one shade (Rule 17.9)

specs.label: Focus
specs.value: 2 px ring, 2 px gap; 3.37 to 1 on Newsprint, 13.29 on Charcoal (Rule 17.9)

specs.label: Loading
specs.value: Words and a still drawing (Rule 17.7)

specs.label: Selected
specs.value: Check, bold words, 2 px edge; in a list, the selected band, its 4 px bar and bold words (Rule 17.10)

specs.label: Warning
specs.value: Warning mark, “Warning:”, 4 px bar in the text’s ink, 13.29 to 1

specs.label: Error
specs.value: Error mark in ink, “Error:”, the fix, 4 px Pillar Red bar; Error Band on Newsprint (text 11.89 to 1), none on Charcoal (bar 4.49 to 1)

specs.label: Empty
specs.value: Dashed region; what is missing and what to do next (Rule 17.12)

specs.label: Success
specs.value: Success mark in Verdigris, 3.37 to 1 on Newsprint and 3.95 on Charcoal, and words

builders: Write a state’s colors with the short names, such as var(--oa-color-state-error-bar) for an error’s 4 px bar and var(--oa-color-surface), never a name that ends in a surface. The theme and the surface classes point each short name at the right value, so the same code draws both columns of this plate.

Draw every state bar as a border, border-left: 4px solid. Forced colors, a setting such as the contrast themes in Windows that repaints a page in a few system colors, removes an inset shadow and keeps a border.

rules.title: Show hover with an underline or an edge and focus with a ring.
rule: Hover underlines a label, grows a link’s underline from 1 to 2 px, or thickens a quiet control’s 1 px edge to 2 px. A quiet control is a button drawn as its word in ink inside that edge, on the page’s own ground. A filled button also steps its fill one shade. Hover never draws an inset shadow, which forced colors removes, and never moves layout.

Focus draws a 2 px ring 2 px outside the control, at once: Verdigris on Newsprint and White, Newsprint on Charcoal and Prussian. On Charcoal the ring around a Newsprint button measures 1.00 to 1 against its fill, so the 2 px gap of Charcoal between them shows the ring. A control whose neighbor stands too close for an outside ring, such as a tab beside the next tab or a row in a list, draws the ring inside its edge with the same 2 px gap, as Rule 18.11 sets.

text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.4.7 Focus Visible asks that keyboard focus always show, and 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) asks that content we place never hide it entirely. A ring outside the control, in a color measured on the surface, shows on every control, filled or not. An underline and an edge are lines in the text’s own ink, so they stay when forced colors repaints the page.

correct.caption: A primary button, a quiet button and a link at rest, on hover and with focus, on Newsprint and on Charcoal. On Charcoal the ring around the Newsprint button is the same color as the button, and the gap shows it.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 17.9. A ring with no gap merges with a Newsprint button on Charcoal, so focus only makes the button 2 px larger. Hover drawn as an inset shadow disappears under forced colors.

specs.label: Hover, words and links
specs.value: Underline; a link’s grows from 1 to 2 px

specs.label: Hover, filled button
specs.value: Fill steps one shade, 1.41 to 1 on Newsprint and 1.41 on Charcoal; label underlines

specs.label: Hover, quiet control
specs.value: Edge from 1 to 2 px, with no shift in size

specs.label: Hover timing
specs.value: At once, or the fast 120 ms

specs.label: Focus ring
specs.value: 2 px outline, at once

specs.label: Focus gap
specs.value: 2 px; never 0. Inside the edge where a neighbor stands too close, offset −4 px (Rule 18.11)

specs.label: Ring color
specs.value: Verdigris on Newsprint 3.37 to 1 and White 4.74; Newsprint on Charcoal 13.29 and Prussian 9.42

builders: Draw the ring with :focus-visible and outline: outline: var(--oa-border-width-focus-ring) solid var(--oa-color-focus-ring); outline-offset: var(--oa-border-focus-offset). Forced colors keeps an outline and removes a box shadow.
When hover thickens an edge, take the extra pixel from the padding, so the control keeps its size and nothing beside it moves.

rules.title: Draw pressed, checked and current choices one way.
rule: A toggle that is pressed, a choice that is checked and the current choice in a set all draw one look: the selected check before the word, the word in bold and a 2 px edge in the strong border color where the others keep 1 px. The look is the same on Newsprint and Charcoal and stays under forced colors, since the check, the weight and the edge are shapes.

Links and lists of places keep their own marks for the current place. A link to the page a reader is on takes bold words, with a 2 px underline in a masthead and none at the end of a breadcrumb, and a rail or a list takes the selected band, its 4 px bar and bold words.

The band holds its words, its bar and, where the row is a choice, a check. On Charcoal the band is Prussian, so a success mark set inside it takes Newsprint, as it does on any Prussian ground, and an error or an ask sits outside the band, since red never sits on Prussian (Rule 05.3).

text: Our pages drew one idea three ways: one switch filled and underlined its choice, one pair turned bold and thickened its edge, and the filter chips added a check. A reader who learns one look reads every control the same way. The check, the weight and the edge carry it without color: the selected band sits only 1.41 to 1 from Newsprint, so the bar beside it does that work in a list.

correct.caption: A pressed toggle, a checked choice, the current page in a list and the current part in a masthead, on Newsprint and on Charcoal.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 17.10. Three controls in one view mark their choice three ways: a fill with an underline, bold words with an underline and a thick edge, and a check with bold words.

specs.label: Check
specs.value: The selected check, 24 px, before the word, in the word’s ink

specs.label: Word
specs.value: Bold, 700; 600 when off

specs.label: Edge
specs.value: 2 px in the strong border color, 13.29 to 1 on Newsprint; 1 px when off

specs.label: Fill
specs.value: The surface’s own ground, on and off

specs.label: Markup
specs.value: aria-pressed="true" on a toggle; a native radio or check box, :checked

specs.label: Current place
specs.value: A link: bold words, with a 2 px underline in a masthead; a rail or list: the selected band, its 4 px bar and bold words

builders: Tie the look to the state the control already holds, [aria-pressed="true"] or :checked, so the drawing always agrees with what a screen reader hears.

rules.title: Keep an unavailable action in reach and say what makes it available.
rule: An action that cannot run yet stays in its place with a dashed edge, readable words and a reason line under it that names the step that makes it available, such as “Choose a size to download.” It keeps focus, so a keyboard reader reaches it, and its accessible description, the line a screen reader reads after its name, carries the reason. Its words take the disabled text token, 5.49 to 1 on Newsprint and 7.26 on Charcoal, and nothing fades.
Form fields stay editable. A Send button that cannot run yet keeps focus and says why under it.

text: A control faded with opacity falls below the contrast its words need: Charcoal at 40 percent measures 2.48 to 1 on Newsprint and 2.61 on White. A button with the disabled attribute also leaves the keyboard’s path, so the reader who most needs the reason never meets it. WCAG 2.2 success criterion 1.4.3 exempts an inactive control’s text from its minimum, and we hold that text to the same 4.5 to 1 as any other words.

correct.caption: A download button before and after a reader chooses a size, on Newsprint and on Charcoal. Before, its reason sits under it, and the button keeps its place in the Tab order.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 17.11. The button is faded to 40 percent, 2.48 to 1, and nothing says why it will not run.

specs.label: Edge
specs.value: Dashed, 1 px

specs.label: Words
specs.value: 5.49 to 1 on Newsprint; 7.26 on Charcoal

specs.label: Reason line
specs.value: Under the control in secondary words, and in its accessible description

specs.label: Markup
specs.value: aria-disabled="true" with aria-describedby to the reason; never the disabled attribute

specs.label: Form fields

rules.title: Say what is missing and what to do next when a region is empty.
rule: A list, table, search or tracker with nothing to show draws a dashed region in place of its rows, and its words say what is missing and the step that would fill it. A search writes both into its status line with the count, so a screen reader hears them together: “0 of 125 symbols. No symbol matches. Clear the search or the filters to see more.”
An empty region names no fault, since nothing failed. When the data fails to arrive, the region shows the error state instead (Rule 11.15).

text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 4.1.3 Status Messages asks that a result such as a count reach a screen reader without moving focus, and a count of 0 alone leaves a reader with nothing to try next. The dashed edge keeps the region at its size, so the page holds still when results return.

correct.caption: A symbol search with no match, on Newsprint and on Charcoal. The dashed edge measures 4.29 to 1 on Newsprint and 7.26 on Charcoal, and the words in it are the status line.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 17.12. “No results.” says nothing about what to try, and the blank space under it looks like a page still loading.
